# New renderings — iliad-084 (13.660–747)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἑλκεχίτωνες (Ἰάονες ἑλκεχίτωνες, 13.685; ἕλκω "drag" + χιτών "tunic") | "trailing-tunicked" | "with trailing tunics" | "long-robed", "with flowing robes", "long-tunicked" (loses ἕλκω "drag"), "trailing-robed"; Ἰάονες is "Ionians", and the unit says they are the Athenians |
| φαιδιμόεις (φαιδιμόεντες Ἐπειοί, 13.686; stock epithet, exact force not known) | "shining" | "shining" | "glorious", "splendid", "radiant", "bright", "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις, "gleaming-eyed"); the note says the sense is not known |
| κῆρ’ ὀλοήν (εὖ εἰδὼς κῆρ’ ὀλοήν, 13.665; κήρ "death-fate", not κῆρ "heart") | "a deadly death-fate" | "the deadly spirit of death" | "deadly doom" ("doom" is turned down for κήρ), "deadly fate" ("fate" is reserved for μοῖρα), "deadly heart" (a different word); κήρ keeps the table’s "death-fate" / "spirit of death" (2.859, 3.360), ὀλοός "deadly" (12.425) |
| θωή (ἀργαλέην θωήν, 13.669; rare) | "penalty" | "penalty" (+ note: the Greek does not say what the penalty was or who would exact it) | "fine", "punishment", "blame", "reproach" (each decides what is unsaid); LSJ glosses "penalty, fine" |
| ὑπὸ γναθμοῖο καὶ οὔατος (13.671) | "beneath the jaw and the ear" | "beneath the jaw and the ear" | "under the ear", "at the angle of the jaw", "behind the jaw" (each moves the place); γναθμός "jaw", οὖς "ear" |
| θυμὸς ᾤχετ’ ἀπὸ μελέων (13.671–672) | "the spirit went from his limbs" | "his spirit left his limbs" | "his life", "his soul" (reserved for ψυχή), "his heart"; follows the table’s θυμὸν ἀπὸ μελέων δῦναι (7.131) |
| στυγερὸς δ’ ἄρα μιν σκότος εἷλεν (13.672) | "and hateful darkness then seized him" | "and hateful darkness seized him" | "covered his eyes" (the formula is σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψε, 4.461, and this is a different line), "black night", "shrouded him"; στυγερὸς σκότος "hateful darkness" (5.47), αἱρέω "seize" |
| τάχα δ’ ἂν καὶ κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν ἔπλετο (13.676–677) | "and soon even the glory of the Achaeans would have been" | "and soon the glory would even have been the Achaeans’" | "victory", "triumph" (κῦδος keeps "glory", 1.405, 1.490), "perhaps" (τάχα can mean "perhaps", but with ἄν and the past tense it is "soon"); ἄν with a past tense is "would have" |
| τοῖος γὰρ γαιήοχος ἐννοσίγαιος ὄτρυν’ Ἀργείους (13.677–678) | "for such an earth-holder, earth-shaker was urging on the Argives" | "for one such as the earth-holder, the earth-shaker, was urging on the Argives" | "Poseidon" (the Greek withholds the name; the note gives it), "so", "thus"; the epithets keep the table’s "earth-holder" and "earth-shaker" (11.241) |
| πρὸς δὲ σθένει αὐτὸς ἄμυνεν (13.678) | "and besides with might himself he defended" | "and he himself added his strength to their defence" | "warded off" (the table keeps it for ἀμύνω with an object), "helped"; ἀμύνω with no object is "defend" |
| ἔχεν ᾗ τὰ πρῶτα πύλας καὶ τεῖχος ἐσᾶλτο (13.679) | "held on, where first he leapt in at the gates and the wall" | "held on at the place where he had first leapt in at the gates and the wall" | "kept his ground", "stayed", "leapt over" (the table’s ἐσᾶλτο πύλας, 12.466, is "leapt in at"); ἔχω with no object is "hold on" |
| πυκινὰς στίχας ἀσπιστάων (13.680) | "the solid ranks of the … shield-bearers" | "the solid ranks of the Danaan shield-bearers" | "close-packed", "thick", "serried" (πυκινός keeps "solid", 4.392); ἀσπιστής "shield-bearer" (8.155) |
| θῖν’ ἔφ’ ἁλὸς πολιῆς εἰρυμέναι (13.682) | "on the shore of the grey sea drawn up" | "stood drawn up on the shore of the grey sea" | "beach", "sand"; the table’s θίς "shore" (11.622), πολιός "grey" (iliad-004, 1.350), ἐρύω "draw up" (4.247–248) |
| χθαμαλώτατον (τεῖχος … χθαμαλώτατον, 13.683) | "lowest" | "lowest" | "most level", "weakest", "lowest of all"; χθαμαλός is "low, near the ground", and the superlative is kept as "lowest" |
| ζαχρηεῖς (13.684; second half of the word not known) | "very violent" | "very violent" | "furious", "raging", "mighty" (reserved for ἴφθιμος); ζα- "very", as in the table’s ζαχρειῶν "very violent" (5.525) |
| σπουδῇ ἐπαΐσσοντα νεῶν ἔχον (13.687) | "with effort held him rushing on from the ships" | "with effort held Hector back from the ships as he rushed on" | "in haste", "eagerly", "hardly" (each decides whether σπουδῇ goes with ἔχον or with ἐπαΐσσοντα); ἔχω with the genitive "keep off from" |
| προλελεγμένοι (13.689; προλέγω "pick out") | "picked men" | "picked men" | "chosen", "champions", "vanguard", "chosen beforehand"; the note says the Ionians are the Athenians |
| Φείδας · Στιχίος · Βίας · Μέγης · Ἀμφίων · Δρακίος · Μέδων · Ποδάρκης (13.691–693) | "Pheidas" · "Stichius" · "Bias" · "Meges" · "Amphion" · "Dracius" · "Medon" · "Podarces" | same | "Phidas", "Stichios", "Dracios"; Stichius, Meges, Medon and Podarces keep the forms already shipped (13.195, 2.627, 2.727, 2.704) |
| Εὐχήνωρ · Πολύϊδος · Κορινθόθι · Ἐρίωπις · Φυλάκη · Ἰφίκλοιο · Φυλακίδαο (13.663–698) | "Euchenor" · "Polyidus" · "at Corinth" · "Eriopis" · "Phylace" · "Iphiclus" · "Phylacus’-son" | "Euchenor" · "Polyidus" · "at Corinth" · "Eriopis" · "Phylace" · "Iphiclus" · "the son of Phylacus" | "Polyeidus" (the Attic spelling), "Eurypis"; Φυλακίδαο follows the table’s Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" / "son of Atreus" and Φυλακίδαο in 2.705 |
| γνωτόν (ἄνδρα κατακτὰς γνωτὸν μητρυιῆς, 13.696–697; a new singular rendering) | "a kinsman" | "a kinsman" | "brother" (the other sense of γνωτός), "relative by blood", "brother-in-law"; the Greek says only "of his stepmother". The table’s γνωτούς (3.174) is "kinsfolk" and turns down "kinsmen" (plural); "kinsfolk" has no singular, so the singular "a kinsman" is chosen here as a new rendering, and "kinsmen" is not used |
| ἄνδρα κατακτάς … ἣν ἔχ’ Ὀϊλεύς (13.696–697) | "having killed a man … whom Oileus had" | "after killing a man … whom Oileus had as his wife" | "murdered" (loads the act), "slain"; κατακτείνω "kill" (table); ἔχω of a wife is "have to wife" |
| ναῦφιν ἀμυνόμενοι (13.700; -φιν "from") | "warding off from the ships" | "in defence of the ships" | "driving off from the ships", "protecting"; ἀμύνω keeps "ward off" (table 4.129) |
| βόε οἴνοπε πηκτὸν ἄροτρον (13.703) | "two wine-faced oxen the jointed plough" | "two oxen with the look of wine … the jointed plough" | "wine-dark" (turned down for the sea, and the same here), "red", "dun"; reused from odyssey-062 (Odyssey 13.31–32) and iliad-061 (πηκτὸν ἄροτρον) |
| ἶσον θυμὸν ἔχοντε (13.704) | "with equal spirit" | "with equal spirit" | "equal heart", "equal strength", "equal courage"; θυμός "spirit" where it is the temper that moves a creature |
| ἀνακηκίει ἱδρώς (13.705; ἀνακηκίω "gush up") | "sweat wells up" | "sweat wells up" | "streams", "pours", "gushes", "drips"; the verb is kept to "wells up" |
| πρυμνοῖσιν κεράεσσι (13.705) | "at the roots of the horns" | "around the roots of their horns" | "tips", "tops", "ends" (πρυμνός is "at the bottom, at the base"); epic dative plural -εσσι |
| ζυγὸν οἶον ἐΰξοον ἀμφὶς ἐέργει (13.706) | "the yoke alone, well-polished, holds apart" | "only the well-polished yoke keeps the two apart" | "divides", "separates"; ἐΰξοος "well-polished" as in the table’s ἐΰξοον (2.390, 4.105) |
| τέλσον ἀρούρης (13.707; τέλσον rare) | "the boundary of the field" | "the field’s boundary" | "the end of the furrow", "the headland" (each decides what the dictionary leaves open), "the border"; ἄρουρα "plough-land" is "field" here as a unit of the plough |
| παρβεβαῶτε … ἕστασαν (13.708) | "having stepped alongside … stood" | "stood close beside each other" | "stood shoulder to shoulder", "stood by each other"; the dual participle of παραβαίνω, literally "having stepped alongside" |
| σάκος ἐξεδέχοντο (13.710) | "his shield took over" | "would take his shield from him" | "carried his shield", "received", "relieved him of"; ἐκδέχομαι "take over from" (the table’s σάκος δ’ ἀνεδέξατο "took" is a different verb) |
| κάματός τε καὶ ἱδρὼς γούναθ’ ἵκοιτο (13.711) | "weariness and sweat should come upon him at the knees" | "weariness and sweat came upon his knees" | "seized", "sank into" (reserved for δύω); κάματος "weariness" (4.230) |
| μίμνε φίλον κῆρ (13.713) | "did the dear heart stay" | "their heart did not hold firm" | "endure", "wait", "remain" (reserved for μίμνω with an object); κῆρ "heart", with φίλον "dear" in `l` and dropped in `i` as in the table |
| ἐϋστρεφεῖ οἶος ἀώτῳ (13.716; the edition prints οἶος, a circumflex) | "well-twisted sheep’s wool" | "well-twisted sheep’s wool" | "alone" (the printed οἶος is a nominative singular with nothing to agree with, so the sense is taken from οἰὸς ἀώτῳ at 13.599), "fleece", "tuft"; follows the shipped 13.599 ("well-twisted sheep’s wool") and the table’s ἄωτος · ἐϋστρεφής |
| ταρφέα βάλλοντες (13.718) | "often casting" | "shooting again and again" | "thickly", "in showers", "in volleys"; ταρφέα keeps the table’s `l` "often" and `i` "again and again" (12.47) |

| ἐλάνθανον βάλλοντες (13.721) | "casting, escaped notice" | "shot without being noticed" | "shot from cover", "unseen", "in secret"; λανθάνω "escape notice" (the table’s λάθεν, 3.420) |

| Ἴλιον ἠνεμόεσσαν (13.724) | "windy Ilios" | "windy Ilios" | "Ilium" (kept for Ἴλιος ἱρή); the table’s ἠνεμόεις "windy" and Ἴλιον "Ilios" (iliad-019, iliad-051) |

| περιίδμεναι ἄλλων (13.728) | "to know beyond others" | "to know more than others" | "surpass others in knowledge", "outdo", "be wiser than"; περίοιδα "know beyond", genitive of comparison |

| κατὰ τεῖχος ἔβησαν (13.737) | "along the wall they went" | "have crossed the wall" | "climbed down", "scaled", "passed through"; κατά "along, over", and the unit’s sense is "got over" |
| ἀφεστᾶσιν σὺν τεύχεσιν (13.738) | "stand apart with their armour" | "stand aloof with their armour" | "stand off", "hold back", "stay out of the fight"; τεῦχος "armour" (table), ἀφίστημι "stand apart" |
| παυρότεροι πλεόνεσσι (13.739) | "fewer against more" | "fewer against more" | "outnumbered" (loses the two comparatives); παῦρος "few" (iliad-025, -046) |
| ἀναχασσάμενος (13.740) | "drawing back" | "fall back" | "retreat", "withdraw", "give ground"; follows the shipped ἀναχασσάμενος "drawing back" / "drew back" (iliad-043, 7.264) and the Odyssey’s "drawing back" |
| πᾶσαν ἐπιφρασσαίμεθα βουλήν (13.741) | "we might well consider the whole plan" | "we could thoroughly consider the whole plan" | "take note of", "notice" (the shipped sense of ἐπιφράζομαι at 2.282, "take note of", where the plan has already been given), "ponder" (reserved for φράζομαι), "devise"; here the object is a plan still to be thought through, so the verb is "consider" — a departure noted here |
| ἐν νήεσσι πολυκλήϊσι πέσωμεν (13.742) | "among the many-thwarted ships we should fall" | "throw ourselves among the ships of many thwarts" | "attack", "fall upon", "storm"; πολυκλήϊσι keeps "many-thwarted" / "of many thwarts" (2.74) and πεσόντες "throw yourselves" (2.175) |

| μίμνει (13.747) | "stays" | "remains" | "waits", "holds firm" (kept for μίμνε of the heart, 713); μίμνω "stay" |

| λαοί (of companions in arms, 13.709–710) | "people" | "troops" | "men", "peoples", "host", "his people" / "good men" (the first draft; "men" and "peoples" are on the table’s avoided list); follows the table’s λαός · λαοί (2.577–580, 3.318): `l` "people", `i` "troops" for an army or fighting band |
| Follows the table unchanged | | | Διῒ φίλος "dear to Zeus", ξεῖνος "guest-friend", ἀφνειός "rich", ἀργαλέος "grievous", νοῦσος "sickness", στυγερός "hateful", χωόμενος "incensed" beside χολόομαι "angered", νόθος "bastard" / "illegitimate", μενεπτόλεμος "steadfast in battle", μεγάθυμος "great-hearted", μεγαλήτωρ "great-spirited", χαλκήρης "bronze-fitted", ἱπποδάσεια "horse-haired" / "thick with horsehair", εὔκυκλος "well-rounded", μείλινος "ashen", δαιδαλέος "wrought" / "finely wrought", χαλκοκορυστής "bronze-armed" / "armed in bronze", θρασύς "bold", δῖος "heavenly", εὐρύοπα Ζεύς "far-thundering Zeus" / "Zeus who thunders from afar", εἶπε παραστάς "spoke, standing beside" / "stood beside … and spoke", ἐν σταδίῃ ὑσμίνῃ "in the standing battle" / "in the battle where men stand their ground" (here without ἐν), ἀμύνω, ῥήγνυμι, φάλαγξ, πεποιθώς "trusting", ἔντεα "gear", δηϊόομαι "be cut down", ἐσάωσε "saved", εὖ εἰδώς "knowing well" |

Reused whole units (identical `l` and `i` to the published ones, as the validator requires): 13.673 (= iliad-069, 11.596) and 13.735 (= iliad-052, 9.103).

Departures from the Odyssey: none. The Odyssey’s half-line βόε οἴνοπε πηκτὸν ἄροτρον (13.32) is reused with its published English.
